newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Africa Israel shareholders okay insurance split.
newsitem.headline: Africa Israel shareholders okay insurance split.

text.p: Shareholders in Africa Israel Investments approved the spin-off of the company's holdings in Leumi Insurance, a company spokesman said on Thursday.
"It was approved by 99.98 percent of the shareholders," he said.
The vote will clear the way for Italian insurer Generali Spa to take control of Leumi Insurance's subsidiary Migdal Insurance, a spokeswoman for Bank Leumi said.
The insurance divestment was a prerequisite for the deal between Bank Leumi and Generali to go ahead. The divestment has already been approved by Africa Israel's board of directors.
Leumi owns 65 percent of the voting rights in Africa Israel, one of Israel's largest holding companies with interests in insurance, construction and tourism.
The bank must reduce its holdings in Africa Israel to 25 percent to comply with Israeli banking law.

Leumi will issue a new tender for its surplus shares in Africa Israel without the insurance holdings, cancelling an earlier tender that had been for Africa Israel together with its insurance holdings, the spokeswoman said.
The accord with Generali convinced Leumi it would get more if it sold Africa Israel and the insurance holdings separately.
Bank Leumi owns 27.72 percent of Leumi Insurance while Africa Israel holds 72.28 percent.
Africa Israel shareholders will receive shares in Leumi Insurance, which will be listed on the bourse.
Leumi Insurance holds 68.1 percent of Migdal, Israel's biggest insurer. Generali owns 27.1 percent and others hold 4.8 percent.
The Generali deal, which is expected to be worth about $300 million, is based on a three billion shekel valuation of Migdal.
